header_summary:
The SHRINCS Working Group has proposed a new cryptographic improvement for Bitcoin, introducing a semi-stateful hash-based signature scheme which is compact and potentially resistant to post-quantum threats. This proposal, still in the prototype phase, requires extensive review and is not yet suitable for production environments. Significant enhancements by Jonas Nick and Mikhail Kudinov aim to increase interoperability and support high-frequency signing applications, although the proposal lacks comprehensive documentation and optimized implementations. The community is encouraged to participate in refining this scheme, with resources and discussions available on GitHub at [SHRINCS.md](https://github.com/SHRINCS/shrincs-bip/blob/main/SHRINCS.md) and an explanatory video at [this link](https://youtu.be/n-jGPICZMR0?si=NpfyTRB88-sUxtlh).

In another development, proposed changes to the testnet5 environment seek to address mining strategy conflicts between CPU and ASIC miners by disabling the min-difficulty rule, which has perpetuated a cycle of strategic future-dated mining. This adjustment, detailed in [this pull request](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35861), aims to stabilize the mining difficulty and restore balance to block generation times, reflecting the dynamic and complex interactions that protocol rules can have on miner behavior and network stability.

Additionally, discussions around BIP34 height encoding in coinbase transactions highlight the increasing space constraints within Bitcoin's transaction data. As block heights grow, encoding requirements could tighten the available space for other transaction elements like the extranonce, underscoring the evolving challenges in blockchain protocol development and the need for careful management of transaction space. More details can be found at [this discussion](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/silent-payments-coinbase/2833/3).

Lastly, a severe denial-of-service vulnerability in Core Lightning's handling of certain peer messages underscored the importance of robust system resource management in cryptocurrency networks. A fix was implemented to prevent unbounded memory consumption by managing the message queue more effectively, detailed in [PR 8525](https://github.com/ElementsProject/lightning/pull/8525). This incident highlights the critical need for continuous security evaluations and updates in the fast-evolving landscape of digital currencies.

recent_posts.title: SHRINCS: an efficient hash-based signature scheme for Bitcoin (first draft)
recent_posts.summary: - The SHRINCS Working Group has introduced a new cryptographic BIP, still in prototype.  - SHRINCS offers rapid verification, public keys at 48 bytes, and security against post-quantum threats.  - The draft lacks critical components like test vectors and optimized implementations for now.

recent_posts.title: Disabling min-difficulty blocks on testnet4
recent_posts.summary: - Recent testnet developments highlight CPU and ASIC miners' strategic conflicts.  - A proposed testnet5 change involves disabling the min-difficulty rule to stabilize mining.  - The ongoing miner conflict under testnet4 rules prevents effective resolution efforts.

recent_posts.title: Silent Payments coinbase
recent_posts.summary:
- The BIP34 height encoding in coinbase scriptSig uses significant transaction data space.
- Four bytes are needed for height encoding, potentially expanding to five bytes.
- Increasing BIP34 encoding costs may limit future extranonce sizes within transactions.

recent_posts.title: Disclosure: Crashing CLN with a flood of pings
recent_posts.summary: - A DoS vulnerability in Core Lightning could crash nodes by exploiting memory issues.  - The issue was resolved by improving `connectd`'s messaging handling and backpressure.  - This incident highlights the importance of robust system design in secure networks.

active_posts.title: A Post-Quantum Path for BIP 324
active_posts.summary:
- Bitcoin's BIP 324 encryption may upgrade to resist quantum computing threats.
- Approaches like hybrid KEM or pure post-quantum KEM are considered for implementation.
- The upgrade aims to boost Bitcoin's security against future quantum decryption risks.

active_posts.title: post-quantum: solution ideas to "tripwire"game-theory issues + a certificate-based rescue protocol
active_posts.summary: - A new UTXO Model Space (NUMS) point could serve as standalone proof of work.  - Group signatures could enhance block proof using post-quantum coin signatures.  - Bitcoin blockchain might be used to publish certificates as quantum proof of ownership.

active_posts.title: Draft BIP for discussion: Time-Shifted Proof of Work (TSPOW) — an informational consensus-design proposal
active_posts.summary:
- The TSPOW protocol proposes a dual-stage mining process adding block producer selection.
- Stability enhancement is claimed by converting block intervals into Gamma-distributed sums.
- Adoption necessitates a hard fork due to major changes in Bitcoin's block structure.

active_posts.title: PQC output type discussion
active_posts.summary: - The email elaborates on adopting P2TRv2 for Bitcoin's quantum threat resilience via PQC.  - Discussions included a long-term shift to P2MR output for complete Bitcoin transition post-CRQC.  - Strategies discussed feature timely ECC-disabling decisions through consensus or hashrate majority.

active_posts.title: Segwit commitment to post-quantum witness data?
active_posts.summary:
- Enhancing blockchain for post-quantum cryptography includes creating an extension block area.
- New blockchain adjustments like pqwtxid integration require major updates to infrastructure.
- Alternatives involve including post-quantum data in segwit areas, affecting storage needs.

active_posts.title: Pragmatic definition of consensus for light clients
active_posts.summary:
- Economic actors validate blockchain value through Proof of Work and future potential.
- Utreexo secures transactions by verifying unspent outputs, ensuring chain integrity despite possible minor losses.
- New light-client protocol enhances security by using block headers to filter and detect forks, recommending action based on fraud detection.
